549Ω fail-safe bias, A to VCC: the largest E96 value keeping idle V_AB ≥ 250 mV over tolerance with a far-end terminator. Idle V_AB is 259 mV nominal, 254 mV worst case; a larger value would let the idle bus sag toward the 200 mV threshold, where receivers read noise.

analyses.description: Idle bus bias and rail current

claims.claim: the idle bus holds V_AB above the receivers' 200 mV threshold with the far end terminated
claims.detail: V_AB ∈ [254, 264] mV over every resistor within 1%

claims.claim: the driver sees no less than the 54 Ω it is specified into
R1 stays within its 250 mW rating with the pair driven to the full 5 V
R2, R3 and R4 stay within their ratings with the pair driven to the opposite rail and DE/RE driven high to transmit
the idle rail stays within its 500 mA budget
claims.detail: 54.6 mA, of which the MCU model is 50 mA

claims.claim: while the MCU pin is not driving it — in reset, and until the firmware sets it — R4 holds DE/RE below the transceiver's 0.8 V V_IL, so the driver stays off
claims.detail: V_DE ≤ 50.5 mV: R4 ≤ 10100 Ω × (1 µA pin leakage + 2 × 2 µA DE/RE input current)

claims.claim: For every R1 from 118.8 Ω to 121.2 Ω (1% resistor); every R2 from 543.51 Ω to 554.49 Ω (1% resistor); every R3 from 543.51 Ω to 554.49 Ω (1% resistor); every far-end terminator from 118.8 Ω to 121.2 Ω (1%, at the other end of the bus), with VCC_5V held at 5 V, the idle bus voltage V(A) − V(B) never falls below 200 mV.

no MCU pin carries two nets, and each hardware UART has one user and is not the console

bom.justification: Arduino Uno MCU as Modbus RTU master: SoftwareSerial TX on D11, RX on D10, direction on D2. Hardware Serial (D0/D1) stays free for uploads and debugging.
bom.price_note: static catalogue price, recorded in the repository on 2026-07-25; when it was first observed is not recorded — not a distributor quote

bom.justification: MAX485 half-duplex transceiver, DE and RE tied to D2: high transmits, low listens. Its supply window is 4.75–5.25 V; a 3.3 V design needs the MAX3485 instead.
120Ω termination across A/B, matching the cable's 120 Ω impedance so edges do not reflect. 1206, not 0402: a driver can put 5 V across it (208 mW), over three times an 0402's rating.

549Ω fail-safe bias, A to VCC: pinned by the requirement (constraints.pinned). Idle V_AB is 259 mV nominal, 254 mV worst case; a larger value would let the idle bus sag toward the 200 mV threshold, where receivers read noise.

549Ω fail-safe bias, B to GND: pinned by the requirement (constraints.pinned). Idle V_AB is 259 mV nominal, 254 mV worst case; a larger value would let the idle bus sag toward the 200 mV threshold, where receivers read noise.

10000Ω pull-down on DE/RE. While the MCU is in reset, and until the firmware sets it, D2 is high-impedance, and a floating DE can switch the driver on and put noise on a bus other nodes are using. This holds the transceiver in receive mode: DE/RE stays at or below 50 mV against the pin's leakage, under the 0.8 V the transceiver reads as low. It draws current only while the pin drives DE high to transmit.

bom.justification: 100nF X7R bypass on U2's supply pin, placed close to it. It supplies the fast edges the rail's trace inductance cannot; without it switching noise couples into every line on the board. Rated 16 V against the 5 V rail.
